en: The Questions of Milinda:
The Introduction to the Book of Puzzles;
The Chapter on the Qualities of a Lay Follower.
2. The Eight Persons Who Destroy Counsel “Venerable Nāgasena, there are these eight persons who, when consulted, ruin the matter under consideration.
Which are the eight?”
"One of lustful temperament, one of hateful temperament, one of deluded temperament, one of proud temperament, the greedy, the lazy,
the single-minded, and the fool— these eight persons spoil a matter that has been deliberated.
Thus spoke the Elder.
“What is their fault?
“Venerable Nāgasena, one of lustful temperament destroys a matter planned through lust; one of hateful temperament destroys a matter planned through hatred;
one of deluded temperament destroys a matter planned through delusion; one of proud temperament—”
One who is malicious ruins a plan conceived out of malice; one who is greedy ruins a plan conceived out of greed;
one who is lazy ruins a plan conceived out of laziness; one who is narrow-minded ruins a plan conceived out of narrow-mindedness;
and one who is foolish ruins a plan conceived out of foolishness.
It is said here:
“One who is lustful, hateful, and deluded;
one who is conceited, greedy, and likewise lazy;”
“One who is single-mindedly intent and one who is foolish—
these two are destroyers of welfare.
These are the eight types of persons who destroy counsel.
